dataRoot.reason: Every check below reads the real archive. Most verify the SHA-256 of source or derived bytes against a bound checksum, which no fixture can reproduce. One asserts the absence of files that no manifest admits, which a fixture cannot demonstrate either, because an empty temporary directory is clean by construction.

detachedSweep.method: Run every check: script from package.json with WITNESS_TREE_DATA_ROOT pointed at a path that does not resolve. The sweep and the checks it spawns then agree on where the archive is meant to be and find it absent, which is what a detached drive looks like to code that goes through the shared resolver.

limits.reason: It asserts the resolved root equals the canonical SSD path, so WITNESS_TREE_DATA_ROOT cannot move it. Pointed at a simulated absent root it read the real 130 GB archive instead and passed, which says nothing about a detached drive. Only a physical detach can observe it.

It sets WITNESS_TREE_DATA_ROOT itself for the subprocesses it drives, so an outer override never reaches them. Its entry here is the registration earned by the earlier physical-detach baseline, not by this sweep.

failingForOtherReasons.name: check:archive-recovery-copy
failingForOtherReasons.reason: data/archive-recovery-copy.json has never been produced. The check fails identically with the archive attached, because it is waiting on an AWS run recorded in docs/ARCHIVE_RECOVERY_COPY_SCHEMA.md, not on the drive.

failingForOtherReasons.name: check:data-root-test-currency
failingForOtherReasons.reason: data/data-root-test-run-receipt.json records a run against a different tree. The check fails identically with the archive attached and is cleared by re-running npm run test:data-root, never by editing the receipt.

failingForOtherReasons.name: check:deployed-map-render
failingForOtherReasons.reason: It renders the deployed site over the network. It fails identically with the archive attached whenever the site is unreachable from this machine.
